summary: Iteration 2 testing: all 25 backend pytest tests pass (auth, languages, movies CRUD, stream, dubbing lifecycle, downloads, deletes incl cascade, validations, analytics). Frontend verified: Movies page renders with Preview/Delete, sidebar 'My Movies' link works, Jobs page has Preview/Download/Delete, Downloads page has all three buttons. Custom VideoPlayer modal opens on Preview click (video element present, play/volume/progress/fullscreen controls visible). Confirmation dialog appears on Delete (text: 'Delete Dubbed Movie - Are you sure...') with Cancel/Delete buttons. Full E2E: upload -> dub (mock ~20s) -> stream -> download (200 OK with video/mp4) -> delete cascade all work. Previously reported user 404 on download could not be reproduced.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 570 lines - consider splitting into routers (auth/movies/dubbing/analytics) before adding more features.
mock_ai_processing uses asyncio.create_task without persistence; if backend restarts mid-job, status stays 'processing' forever. Add a startup recovery sweep to mark stale processing jobs as failed.
CORS allow_origins falls back to '*' with allow_credentials=True - not spec-compliant; recommend explicit origins list.
Stream endpoints return entire FileResponse without Range/206 support - large files won't allow video seeking efficiently. Consider StreamingResponse with Range header support for production.
delete_movie: file deletion errors (e.g., permission) are not try/except wrapped - could 500 mid-cascade leaving DB inconsistent.
seed_data_creation: Created test user + session; uploaded TEST_movie2.mp4 multiple times during tests (cleaned up via delete tests).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth via cookie 'session_token' (httpOnly/secure/sameSite=None) on voicecinema-1.preview.emergentagent.com OR Bearer header. Mock dubbing pipeline takes ~20s. VideoPlayer modal opens via Preview buttons on Jobs/Downloads/Movies. ConfirmDialog shows on Delete. Download endpoint returns 200 with video/mp4 - the user-reported 404 could not be reproduced; likely it was due to a deleted job or stale frontend state.
rca of the issue: User-reported 404 on download could not be reproduced. Backend logs confirm 200 OK. Likely root cause: user attempted download after deleting the job/movie, or before completion, or used stale UI state. Backend now logs detailed errors (job_id, file path, exists check) which will catch any real future occurrence.
